en.title: Obsidian Director Fires Back at 'Cold Take Artists' Over Studio's Identity
en.summary: Amidst recent layoffs and a reported shift in development focus, Obsidian's Brandon Adler is pushing back against what he calls "staggering" misinformation about the studio's supposed decline. He asserts the core creative DNA remains intact, linking current projects directly to the studio's storied past.
en.body:
The gaming landscape is constantly shifting, and with it, the narratives surrounding beloved studios. Following recent news of significant layoffs at Microsoft-owned **Obsidian Entertainment** and a reported pivot for the studio to focus on a new **Fallout** title, speculation about the studio's internal state has run rampant online. Many have voiced concerns that **Obsidian** is no longer the same creative force that delivered classics like **Knights of the Old Republic 2** and **Fallout: New Vegas**. However, **Brandon Adler**, a game director at **Obsidian**, is speaking out against these claims, which he believes are largely misinformed.

Adler took to LinkedIn to express his frustration with what he terms "cold take artists" who, he argues, lack a fundamental understanding of the studio's history and its people. He stated, "The number of times I've seen people, with no understanding of who has worked on our previous games or what they contributed, talk about how **Obsidian** isn't who they used to be... is staggering. Most of the time they are not just wrong, but spreading an enormous amount of misinformation." He emphasized that many key individuals in leadership roles today are the same ones who shaped **Obsidian**'s earlier acclaimed titles.

## The Enduring Obsidian DNA

Adler's core argument is that the studio's foundational creative spirit, its "DNA," has remained remarkably consistent. He directly refutes the notion that **Obsidian** has lost its original talent, pointing out the continuity of personnel. "Like, literally the same people," he wrote. "The through line from **KotOR 2** to our current games is pretty clear." This assertion suggests that while the studio has undoubtedly evolved and adapted to new platforms and projects, the underlying creative vision and the talent pool responsible for its legacy are still very much present. He further elaborated that this same DNA is what created beloved titles such as **Knights of the Old Republic**, **Fallout: New Vegas**, **Neverwinter Nights 2**, and **South Park: The Stick of Truth**.

## Fan Reaction and Future Focus

This defense comes at a critical time for **Obsidian**, as the studio navigates industry-wide restructuring and the reported cancellation of an *Avowed* sequel in favor of the new **Fallout** project. For fans who cherish **Obsidian**'s particular brand of narrative-driven, choice-heavy RPGs, the continuity of talent is paramount. The idea that the studio's soul might be lost would be a significant blow. Adler's comments aim to reassure the community that the passion and expertise that defined **Obsidian**'s past successes are still the driving force behind its future endeavors, particularly with the highly anticipated return to the **Fallout** universe.

## What's Next

While specific details regarding the new **Fallout** title remain scarce, **Obsidian**'s commitment to its core strengths appears stronger than ever. Fans can anticipate further updates on **Obsidian**'s projects as development progresses, with the studio clearly signaling its intent to continue delivering the kind of deep, engaging RPG experiences its audience expects.

content_raw: Earlier this month, Microsoft announced "the most significant restructure in Xbox history", which is what you call it when you lay off thousands of people and cut four game studios loose . Double Fine and Compulsion Games returned to their indie roots; Ninja Theory and Undead Labs were sold off. While it seemed at first like Obsidian Entertainment had avoided the headsman's axe, we soon found out they were also hit with plenty of layoffs of their own . We also found out someone apparently pushed the button marked "in case of emergency get Obsidian to make a new Fallout game," with Fallout: New Vegas director Josh Sawyer reportedly heading the project . So a mix of good news and bad there. Online, the response has included plenty of suggestions that Obsidian "already kind of gutted all the original writers and talent that made old Obsidian games what they were" and that it wasn't the same studio as the one that made games like the original New Vegas or Knights of the Old Republic 2. Brandon Adler, a game director at Obsidian, disputed these claims on LinkedIn , saying, "The number of times I've seen people, with no understanding of who has worked on our previous games or what they contributed, talk about how Obsidian isn't who they used to be... is staggering. Most of the time they are not just wrong, but spreading an enormous amount of misinformation." As Adler explained, plenty of people in leadership roles at Obsidian are the same people now as they were in the past. "Like, literally the same people", he wrote. "The through line from KotOR2 to our current games is pretty clear." Of course, that doesn't mean the studio hasn't changed. "But the DNA at Obsidian is the same as it always was. The same DNA that created KotOR, New Vegas, NWN2, and Stick of Truth." Personally, I'm interested in whatever Obsidian does next because Pentiment was a masterpiece, and seeing people confidently declare that a new Fallout game from Obsidian would be a disaster because they personally didn't care for The Outer Worlds 2 seems like a bit of a stretch. Adler also noted that it has been a tough time for the studio, for the obvious reasons. "This has been an extremely difficult week at Obsidian", he wrote. "Not only have I had to say goodbye to some amazing game developers, but I've had to say goodbye to some of my best friends. I truly feel for every one of them. Know that if you are looking to hire one of these former Obsidian devs, you are hiring some of the best people around – both professionally and personally."
